brief: Morgan Stanley argues the equity correction that began mid-2026 is in its final phase. The cap-weighted S&P 500 is catching down to already improved breadth, with the equal-weight S&P outperforming the cap-weighted index by about 6% and the Russell 2000 by about 4% since September as 10-year yields fell nearly 40bp. The firm wants either its sentiment indicator to reach capitulation levels, or the S&P 500 to hit its 7100 to 7300 downside target, before adding risk more aggressively. Its year-end base case stays 8000. Three clearing events could resolve the overhang. On financial conditions, Fed Chair Warsh stopped short of calling conditions outright tight, leaving room for a Treasury General Account drawdown or lighter issuance to ease liquidity. On midterms, a Democrat sweep is already priced in with its magnitude uncertain, seasonality historically favors large caps after midterms, though renewed Iran escalation or new tariffs are flagged as the bigger post-election risk. On earnings, free cash flow surprises are driving larger price reactions than EPS surprises this quarter, reinforcing the firm's quality-cyclical tilt, with Industrials as its top pick.
